_doc: Garsoore import clearance. This replaces the flat 5% duty the catalogue used to apply to everything.
STATUS IS LOAD-BEARING, exactly as it is on the rate cards. 'draft' means NOBODY HAS CONFIRMED THESE NUMBERS.
They are structurally correct and numerically unverified: a licensed Somali clearing agent has to sit down with
this file and replace every rate and fee with what is actually charged at the port and the airport. Until then
the shop is quoting an assumption, and the admin console says so.
What IS reliable here is the shape, and the shape is what the flat 5% got wrong:
1. Duty is assessed on CIF - the value of the goods PLUS the freight to get them here - not on the goods alone.
2. The rate is not one number. It varies by what the thing is.
3. A large part of clearing a shipment costs the SAME whether the box holds one phone or four hundred:
the clearing agent, the delivery order, the documents, terminal handling. Those are per-shipment costs and
they are shared across the basket like freight is, not charged per item. Charging them per item was the
same mistake that made a $6 shirt cost $24.
Anything a clearing agent tells you that is not in this file is missing from the customer's price.

dutyBands._doc: Ad valorem rate applied to CIF, per catalogue category. Every one of these needs a broker's confirmation.

_doc: Fixed cost of clearing ONE consignment through the port or the airport, whatever is inside it.
Read the next part carefully, because getting it wrong is how a $6 shirt ends up priced at $98.
Garsoore does not clear one consignment per customer. The China facility consolidates many customers' goods
into one shipment and clears it once. So a single customer must pay a SHARE of these fees, proportional to
how much of the consignment is theirs - not the whole thing. The share is worked out by dividing these fees
by 'typical', the consignment size we actually expect to move, giving a per-kg (air) or per-CBM (sea) loading.
'typical' is therefore an OPERATING ASSUMPTION, not a contract term, and it is the most important number on
this page: set it too high and every order is underpriced, too low and nobody buys. Revisit it against real
consignment weights once a few have actually shipped - the admin console shows what it is currently set to.

excluded: storage or demurrage once free time at the port expires
anything requiring a permit (pharmaceuticals, weapons, some chemicals)
notes: Duty is charged on CIF, so raising the freight raises the duty - the two are not independent.
Categories that may not sit at the default rate once a broker looks: vehicles and parts, solar equipment (often
relieved or reduced as capital/energy goods), and building materials. Ask about these three specifically.
If any category turns out to be relieved from duty entirely, set it to 0 here rather than deleting the line, so
it is visible that somebody checked.
